\textbf{\large Infinite Series Worksheet (9.3) --- Solutions}

\vspace{4pt}

\typehead{Type A: Geometric Series}{$\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} ar^k = a + ar + ar^2 + \cdots$ converges to $\dfrac{a}{1-r}$ if $|r|<1$ and diverges if $|r|\ge 1$. Here $a$ is always the \emph{first term} and $r$ is the ratio of consecutive terms.}

\problem{1.}{\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{7}{3^{k}}}

Geometric with $a = 7$ and $r = \frac{1}{3}$. Since $|r| = \frac13 < 1$, the series converges and
$\displaystyle \frac{a}{1-r} = \frac{7}{1-\frac13} = \frac{7}{2/3} = \frac{21}{2}.$
\answer{converges, sum $= \frac{21}{2}$}

\problem{2.}{\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{k}\, 6}{5^{k}}}

Rewrite as $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} 6\left(-\tfrac15\right)^{k}$: geometric with $a = 6$, $r = -\frac15$. Since $|r| = \frac15 < 1$, it converges and
$\displaystyle \frac{a}{1-r} = \frac{6}{1+\frac15} = \frac{6}{6/5} = 5.$
\answer{converges, sum $= 5$}

\problem{3.}{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} 2^{2k}\, 3^{1-k}}

Concealed form:
$\displaystyle \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} 2^{2k}\,3^{1-k} = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{4^{k}}{3^{k-1}} = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} 4\left(\frac43\right)^{k-1}.$
Since $r = \frac43 > 1$, the series diverges.
\answer{diverges}

\problem{4.}{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{5^{k+1}}{8^{k}}}

$\displaystyle \frac{5^{k+1}}{8^k} = \frac{5^2\cdot 5^{k-1}}{8\cdot 8^{k-1}} = \frac{25}{8}\left(\frac58\right)^{k-1}$, so $a = \frac{25}{8}$ and $r = \frac58$. Since $|r|<1$, it converges and
$\displaystyle \frac{a}{1-r} = \frac{25/8}{3/8} = \frac{25}{3}.$
\answer{converges, sum $= \frac{25}{3}$}

\problem{5.}{\sum_{k=2}^{\infty} \frac{3^{k}}{2^{3k-1}}}

$\displaystyle \frac{3^k}{2^{3k-1}} = \frac{2\cdot 3^k}{8^k} = 2\left(\frac38\right)^{k}$. The first term ($k=2$) is $a = \frac{9}{32}$ and $r = \frac38$, $|r|<1$, so
$\displaystyle \frac{a}{1-r} = \frac{9/32}{5/8} = \frac{9}{32}\cdot\frac{8}{5} = \frac{9}{20}.$
\answer{converges, sum $= \frac{9}{20}$}

\problem{6.}{3 + \frac{3}{4} + \frac{3}{4^{2}} + \cdots + \frac{3}{4^{k-1}} + \cdots}

This is $\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} 3\left(\frac14\right)^{k-1}$: geometric with $a = 3$, $r = \frac14$. Since $|r|<1$, it converges and
$\displaystyle \frac{a}{1-r} = \frac{3}{3/4} = 4.$
\answer{converges, sum $= 4$}

\problem{7.}{\frac{2}{9} - \frac{4}{27} + \frac{8}{81} - \cdots + \frac{(-1)^{k-1}\,2^{k}}{3^{k+1}} + \cdots}

$\displaystyle \frac{(-1)^{k-1}2^k}{3^{k+1}} = \frac{2}{9}\left(-\frac23\right)^{k-1}$ (check: each term is $-\frac23$ times the previous one), so $a = \frac29$, $r = -\frac23$, $|r|<1$:
$\displaystyle \frac{a}{1-r} = \frac{2/9}{5/3} = \frac{2}{15}.$
\answer{converges, sum $= \frac{2}{15}$}

\newpage

\typehead{Type B: Telescoping Sums}{Write $s_n$ in closed form, then $\sum_{k=1}^\infty u_k = \lim_{n\to+\infty} s_n$ (if the limit exists).}

\problem{8.}{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{k^{2}+3k+2}}

$\displaystyle \frac{1}{(k+1)(k+2)} = \frac{1}{k+1} - \frac{1}{k+2}$, so
$\displaystyle s_n = \left(\tfrac12 - \tfrac13\right) + \left(\tfrac13 - \tfrac14\right) + \cdots + \left(\tfrac{1}{n+1} - \tfrac{1}{n+2}\right) = \frac12 - \frac{1}{n+2} \;\longrightarrow\; \frac12.$
\answer{converges, sum $= \frac12$}

\problem{9.}{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(2k-1)(2k+1)}}

$\displaystyle \frac{1}{(2k-1)(2k+1)} = \frac12\left(\frac{1}{2k-1} - \frac{1}{2k+1}\right)$, so
$\displaystyle s_n = \frac12\left[\left(1 - \tfrac13\right) + \left(\tfrac13 - \tfrac15\right) + \cdots + \left(\tfrac{1}{2n-1} - \tfrac{1}{2n+1}\right)\right] = \frac12\left(1 - \frac{1}{2n+1}\right) \to \frac12.$
\answer{converges, sum $= \frac12$}

\problem{10.}{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \ln\!\left(\frac{k}{k+1}\right)}

$\ln\!\left(\frac{k}{k+1}\right) = \ln k - \ln(k+1)$, so
$\displaystyle s_n = (\ln 1 - \ln 2) + (\ln 2 - \ln 3) + \cdots + (\ln n - \ln(n+1)) = -\ln(n+1) \to -\infty.$
\answer{diverges}

\problem{11.}{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{2}{k(k+2)}}

$\displaystyle \frac{2}{k(k+2)} = \frac1k - \frac{1}{k+2}$. Terms cancel two apart:
$$
s_n = \left(1 - \tfrac13\right) + \left(\tfrac12 - \tfrac14\right) + \left(\tfrac13 - \tfrac15\right) + \cdots + \left(\tfrac{1}{n-1} - \tfrac{1}{n+1}\right) + \left(\tfrac1n - \tfrac{1}{n+2}\right)
= 1 + \frac12 - \frac{1}{n+1} - \frac{1}{n+2} \to \frac32.
$$
\answer{converges, sum $= \frac32$}

\problem{12.}{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{4}{k^{2}+4k+3}}

$\displaystyle \frac{4}{(k+1)(k+3)} = \frac{2}{k+1} - \frac{2}{k+3}$. Terms cancel two apart:
$$
s_n = 2\left[\left(\tfrac12 - \tfrac14\right) + \left(\tfrac13 - \tfrac15\right) + \cdots + \left(\tfrac{1}{n+1} - \tfrac{1}{n+3}\right)\right]
= 2\left(\frac12 + \frac13 - \frac{1}{n+2} - \frac{1}{n+3}\right) \to \frac53.
$$
\answer{converges, sum $= \frac53$}

\problem{13.}{\frac{1}{4\cdot 5} + \frac{1}{5\cdot 6} + \frac{1}{6\cdot 7} + \cdots + \frac{1}{(k+3)(k+4)} + \cdots}

This is $\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(k+3)(k+4)}$ with $\frac{1}{(k+3)(k+4)} = \frac{1}{k+3} - \frac{1}{k+4}$, so
$\displaystyle s_n = \left(\tfrac14 - \tfrac15\right) + \left(\tfrac15 - \tfrac16\right) + \cdots + \left(\tfrac{1}{n+3} - \tfrac{1}{n+4}\right) = \frac14 - \frac{1}{n+4} \to \frac14.$
\answer{converges, sum $= \frac14$}

\problem{14.}{\frac{1}{1\cdot 4} + \frac{1}{4\cdot 7} + \frac{1}{7\cdot 10} + \cdots + \frac{1}{(3k-2)(3k+1)} + \cdots}

This is $\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(3k-2)(3k+1)}$ with $\frac{1}{(3k-2)(3k+1)} = \frac13\left(\frac{1}{3k-2} - \frac{1}{3k+1}\right)$, so
$\displaystyle s_n = \frac13\left[\left(1 - \tfrac14\right) + \left(\tfrac14 - \tfrac17\right) + \cdots + \left(\tfrac{1}{3n-2} - \tfrac{1}{3n+1}\right)\right] = \frac13\left(1 - \frac{1}{3n+1}\right) \to \frac13.$
\answer{converges, sum $= \frac13$}
